note: Files: S3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (base, cue) and r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl (RL, plain), fetched to runs/theory-tests/s3/. Both have 500 rows, one per problem_index, sample 0, cap_hit always a bool and no empty text. Rows with cap_hit false are kept, and all eligible occurrences are pooled per model. Commas are deleted between digits before the hold-on and number matching, so s and e are positions in the comma-free text. Main reading: the last number in before and the first number in after are compared as exact strings. alt_measured compares them by numeric value (float), so '0.5' equals '0.50'. The number regex has no sign, so '-3' and '3' count as the same number in both readings. It also splits decimals like '.5' and treats digits inside LaTeX such as \frac{1}{2} or x^2 as numbers, so 'revision' is a coarse text proxy. The windows are 300/400 characters and can include the problem restatement or the cue text (text starts with ' line!'). The script prints a '#' line with the counts before the JSON. If the RL rate is 0 or either model has no eligible occurrence, the script reports not_computable.

Files: S3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl joined by problem_index to the committed studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json (500 entries, t1_right 0/1, grader v3). The script uses the row's own cap_hit field, not t1_cap_hit. s_last is the start of the last hold-on match in the original text. The prefix text[:s_last] is cut first and its digit commas deleted afterwards; the answer's digit commas are deleted after normalization. Normalization strips whitespace, removes every '$', and unwraps \boxed{...} only when the brace opened by \boxed closes at the last character. Main reading: the answer counts as present only where the characters on both sides are not ASCII [A-Za-z0-9] (string edges count). alt_measured counts any plain substring occurrence. Rows whose answer is empty after normalization are dropped; the '#' line reports how many. Extracted answers are raw strings, so an answer that appears earlier in a different form (for example \frac{1}{2} vs 1/2, or \dfrac) counts as not kept. This lowers the fraction. Short answers like '2' match easily, which raises it. 32 to 38 T1 rows have no extracted answer and are dropped when both extracted fields are empty.

Files: S3 r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base, cue) and .../abaybektursun-1114-151540-86ef/answers.jsonl (RL, plain), fetched to runs/theory-tests/<job-id>/. Each has 328 rows with score_v3 0/1 present in the rows, so no regrading is done. Rows with cap_hit false are kept; right means score_v3 == 1 and wrong means anything else. An empty text gets density 0 (none were seen). Main reading: the mean of per-row densities in each group. alt_measured pools per group: total matches / (total characters / 1000). The recipe's undefined case (no finished-wrong rows, no finished-right rows, or a right mean of 0) prints measured null with refuted_by_met true. R_RL = 0 (RL wrong rows have no hold-ons) is also treated as undefined, which the recipe does not state explicitly. Density uses characters of text, which includes the cue text at the start of the base rows. Base has about 75 rows with no extracted answer, all wrong under v3; finished ones among them enter the wrong group even if they are format failures. The theory's scope excludes format failures, but the recipe does not filter them out.
